# Fixtures for the WhatsApp providers

Sample payloads for `gupshup.ts`, `webhooks.ts` (messages and statuses) and `statuses.ts`. None of them came from a call to a real service: nothing in this folder has touched Gupshup or Meta.

**Copied from Gupshup's partner documentation, read on 11 Nov 2026.** Changes from the pages: customers' numbers became `919800000001` and profile names became `CUSTOMER_NAME`. The ids, timestamps, error codes and structure are as published. Where the page writes a number as a string or as a number, the fixture keeps the page's choice.

- `gupshup-v3-status-set-callback.json`, `-enqueued.json`, `-sent.json`, `-delivered.json`, `-read.json`, `-failed.json`, `-failed-internal.json`, `gupshup-v3-message-audio.json`, `gupshup-v3-message-image.json`, `gupshup-v3-message-call-permission-reply.json` come from https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/docs/events (updated 30 Oct 2026). These are the "V3" events: Meta's body plus `gs_app_id`, with `gs_id` on statuses. "Failed (internal)" is Gupshup's own refusal before Meta saw the message. It has no wamid, no metadata and no `gs_app_id`.
- `gupshup-v3-message-text.json` and `gupshup-v3-status-read-passthrough.json` come from https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/docs/whatsapp-passthrough-apis-for-partners (updated 21 Jul 2026). In that page's status example, `id` is a second UUID and not a wamid, while the events page has a wamid there. This is why the parser keeps both ids and the record is searched for either.
- `gupshup-v3-send-reply.json`, `gupshup-error-authentication.json` and `gupshup-error-callback-billing.json` come from https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/docs/whatsapp-passthrough-apis-for-partners (the reply's id) and https://partner-docs.gupshup.io/reference/post_partner-app-appid-v3-text-message (the error bodies, the same on every v3 message page).

**Copied from Meta's documentation, read on 11 Nov 2026:**

- `meta-status-failed.json` comes from https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status.md ("a message that failed to be sent"). Meta's delivered example is in `templates/commerce/bookings/test/fixtures/whatsapp-webhook-status-delivered.json`.

**What Gupshup's docs do not show:** a v3 callback for a tapped reply button or list row. The tests wrap Meta's own examples (`templates/commerce/bookings/test/fixtures/whatsapp-webhook-button-reply.json` and `-list-reply.json`) in Gupshup's `gs_app_id`. The call-permission reply above shows Gupshup keeping Meta's `interactive` object as Meta writes it. A real Gupshup app must confirm this (Deferred.md).

**Gupshup self-serve (item 11c), read on 12 Nov 2026 on docs.gupshup.io.** The `gupshup-selfserve-*` files. As with the partner files, nothing here came from a call to a real service. Customers' numbers are `919800000001`, names `CUSTOMER_NAME`, links `example.invalid`. The pages quote JSON only in part (the fetch tool I read them with summarised them), so each file says below how far it is the page's own text and how far it is shaped from the page's field list. A real Gupshup app must confirm every one (Deferred.md).

- `gupshup-selfserve-send-reply.json`: the success body "status submitted, messageId" with the page's own example id. https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/template-messages.md and https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/session-text-message.md (the text page lists 200 submitted, 400 "Invalid Destination" or "Invalid App Details", 401 authentication failed, 429 too many requests).
- `gupshup-selfserve-error-invalid-destination.json`, `-error-invalid-app.json`: the two 400 messages the text page names, in the `{ status: "error", message }` shape it gives.
- `gupshup-selfserve-templates.json`: the template list. The fields (`id`, `elementName`, `languageCode`, `status`, `templateType`, `data`, `category`) and the top-level `status: "success"` are from https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/get-all-templates-for-an-app.md (the page gives one example template, `event_test`; the four here are written to our names). The older route `GET /sm/api/v1/template/list/{appname}` (https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/getalltemplatesforanapp) shows no response body at all, so its reply is assumed to be the same.
- `gupshup-selfserve-message-text.json`, `-image.json`, `-audio.json`: the version 2 envelope `app`, `timestamp` (ms), `version`, `type: "message"`, `payload { id, source, type, payload, sender }` as https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/text.md and https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/media.md describe it (image: `caption`, `url`, `contentType`, `urlExpiry`; audio: `url`, `contentType`, `urlExpiry`). Shaped from the field lists.
- `gupshup-selfserve-message-list-reply.json`: the list reply example on https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/interactive, with our own `postbackText` value (the page's is "section 1 row 1 postback payload"; ours is an id our code made).
- `gupshup-selfserve-message-quick-reply.json`: a tapped reply button. The interactive page shows `quick_reply` with `payload { title, id, reply }` (for example "First", "qr1", "First 1"); the `postbackText` beside them is from https://docs.gupshup.io/reference/postback-text-support.md, which shows the postback arriving in a template button's reply. Whether a session quick reply carries it is NOT shown by any page: `-quick-reply-no-postback.json` is the page's own three fields, and the parser reads it as ordinary words.
- `gupshup-selfserve-event-enqueued.json`, `-sent.json`, `-delivered.json`, `-read.json`, `-failed.json`: https://docs.gupshup.io/docs/message-events.md ("V2 message events"): `type: "message-event"`; `id` is Gupshup's id on enqueued and failed and WhatsApp's on sent, delivered and read, with `gsId` (Gupshup's) beside it on those; `payload.ts` is Meta's time in seconds; a failure has `payload { code, reason }` (the page's examples are 1008 "User is not Opted in and Inactive" and 470). The ids here are the page's placeholders made into values.
